To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a dairy herd health program is a valuable tool for improving the health and productivity of dairy herds.
the incidence of clinical disease in dairy cattle in Australia is 43.4 per cent per 100 animal years.
the average incidence of disease in commercial dairy herds was 43.4 incidents per 100 animals per year.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a health program for commercial dairying herds.
the application of epidemiology to the control of disease in dairy herds.
the development of a practical and cost effective approach for the control of specific disease entities in commercial dairy herds, and for the management of the herd as a whole.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the incidence of specific disease entities was similar to other published data.
the disease incidence and the level of disease control in these herds were not as high as they could be.
disease is the major factor affecting herd productivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the incidence of disease was high, the incidence of disease-related death was low, the incidence of management-related death was low and the incidence of voluntary culling was high.
the incidence of specific diseases was similar to that found in other Australian studies, but that the incidence of disease was lower than found in other countries.
the average dairy herd in this study had an incidence of 43.5 disease incidents per year, with a total of 9.9% of the cows being disposed of for disease reasons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more aware of the importance of mastitis and infertility in dairy herds.
the occurrence of specific disease is not a reliable indicator of the success or failure of a herd health program.
the occurrence of disease in dairy cattle can be reduced through the use of a herd health program, and that the incidence of disease can be used to monitor the effectiveness of such a program.
